answer: A harbor registry admits agents only after random mutual audits. Each epoch a beacon pairs each newcomer with an unrelated auditor who replays one job log for a 20-credit stake. A willow rule bends without breaking: one disputed log earns a second audit, not exile. The k-th fake still needs its own 50-credit bond, log, and auditor, so 1,000 fakes risk 50,000 credits with no bulk discount; an honest agent pays 50 once. Remote tundra auditors get a 24-hour filing window. Named failure mode: auditor collusion, blocked because pairs are drawn fresh each epoch.
